title: Post hoc amendment 2: hyperparameter sensitivity of the Random Forest, group spectra and the montage error map
status: post hoc: decided after the results of notebooks 02-06 were seen; outside the reading rules of the analysis plan; descriptive

amends.note: The analysis plan is not edited (its hash stays the same); this amendment has its own hash and is frozen by notebooks 10 and 11 before they compute anything. Amendment 1 (config/post_hoc_plan.json) is unchanged.

rationale: The hyperparameters of the Random Forest were fixed in the plan and never tuned, to avoid optimistic estimates. Reviewers may ask whether the conclusions depend on that choice. Part A re-runs the frozen pipeline with a small grid of hyperparameters, changed one at a time, and reports every configuration without choosing the best. Parts B and C are descriptive figures of the harmonised data: the group-average power spectra and the angular error of the BrainLat 10-20 correspondence.

A_hyperparameter_sensitivity.question: Do discrimination, incremental value and transport depend on the Random Forest hyperparameters fixed in the plan?
A_hyperparameter_sensitivity.reference: the frozen configuration of the plan (n_estimators 300, max_depth none, max_features sqrt, min_samples_leaf 1, bootstrap, class_weight balanced, random_state 42)
A_hyperparameter_sensitivity.design: one hyperparameter changed at a time; everything else as in the plan (11 features, 19 channels, epoch-level training, subject P(AD) = mean over epochs, same seed, same standardisation)
A_hyperparameter_sensitivity.validation: the same leave-one-subject-out within each cohort as notebook 02; transport as in notebook 05 (trained on the whole source cohort, applied once to the other)

metrics.within_cohort: AUC of the EEG score with bootstrap 95% CI (2000 resamples, stratified, seed 42)
metrics.incremental_value: OR per 1 SD of the EEG score beyond the covariates of the cohort, profile-likelihood 95% CI, and the likelihood-ratio statistic; no p-value (the null bootstrap is too expensive to repeat and the naive p is liberal)
metrics.transport: AUC in the other cohort with bootstrap 95% CI, and the calibration slope

A_hyperparameter_sensitivity.check: the frozen configuration must reproduce the predictions of notebooks 02 and 05 exactly
A_hyperparameter_sensitivity.selection: none: no configuration is chosen; all are reported (Table S11, Fig. S5)

B_group_spectra.question: What do the harmonised spectra look like, by cohort and diagnosis?
B_group_spectra.method: the same reading and preprocessing as the features (19 channels, average reference, 40 Hz low-pass of the Greek data, 0.5-45 Hz FIR, 4-s epochs, RMS normalisation); Welch spectrum of each epoch with the same 1 Hz resolution, averaged over the 19 channels and divided by its power in 0.5-45 Hz (relative spectral density); mean over the epochs of each participant
B_group_spectra.participants: the participants with analysable EEG (as in the analyses)
B_group_spectra.summary: mean of the participants of each group with a bootstrap 95% interval (participants resampled; 2000 resamples; seed 42)
B_group_spectra.sharing: only group curves are written to the files meant for sharing; participant spectra stay in outputs/descriptive/

C_montage_error_map.method: the BrainLat electrode positions and the 10-20 positions used by notebook 01 (same functions, same file), projected on the head; each 10-20 position coloured by the angle to its BioSemi electrode
C_montage_error_map.reference_spacing: angle between each 10-20 position and its nearest 10-20 neighbour, to compare with the errors

reporting: Labelled 'post hoc' (part A) or 'descriptive' (parts B and C) wherever it appears. None of it changes a reading of RQ1-RQ3.
